title: Probing-augmented change-point attribution and rollback budgeter
author: Marina Cortez
description:
Motivation: We currently detect regressions using aggregated canary metrics which can conflate unrelated phase shifts (traffic mix, seq-len, cold-KV hits) and lead to noisy rollbacks or missed regressions. This PR adds a lightweight synthetic probing layer that augments live traffic signals to attribute change-points to workload-shift vs. model/runtime regressions, and budgets rollback impact via a credit-based controller.

Summary of changes: adds a probing controller that schedules small targeted synthetic probes across temporal cohorts, collects phase-aligned latency/throughput fingerprints, and runs a probabilistic attribution pass to decide whether a detected change-point is correlated with workload change or intrinsic regression. Introduces a rollback budgeter that consumes credits on each automatic rollback and replenishes based on sustained stability.

Why this is different: unlike the existing canary detectors that compare time-windowed aggregates, the probing layer performs active micro-experiments against representative slices (by seq-length, prompt-type, region) which exposes regressions that only manifest under specific slice conditioning. The attribution model is probabilistic and returns an attribution score used by the rollout controller to gate automated rollbacks. The budgeter prevents oscillation by quantifying acceptable rollback spend per deployment window.

Files touched (high level):
- runtime/canary/probing_controller.py: probe scheduler & coordinator (core logic)
- runtime/canary/attribution_model.py: lightweight Bayesian learner used for attribution scoring
- runtime/canary/rollback_budgeter.go: rollback credit accounting and replenishment policy
- ops/canary/configs/probing_profiles.yaml: default cohort profiles and probe budgets
- console/canary_ui/attribution_panel.tsx: UI surface to inspect probe fingerprints and attribution traces
- tests/perf/test_probing_integration.py: integration tests that simulate phase shifts and model regressions
- ci/perf_canary_pipeline.yml: pipeline additions to validate probing logic end-to-end

Implementation notes:
- The probe scheduler emits micro-traffic with adaptive inter-probe spacing to avoid adding meaningful load; probes are pinned to lower-priority lanes.
- Attribution_model uses a conjugate prior on latency deltas across cohorts and incorporates probe-vs-live correlation; returns attributes: WORKLOAD, RUNTIME, MODEL with confidence.
- Rollback_budgeter implemented in Go to integrate with existing rollout controller: each automatic rollback deducts credits; manual rollback does not. Credits are replenished by time-decayed stability (no automatic rollbacks for X hours) and by successful canary passes.
- Added feature flags (canary.probing.enabled, canary.attribution.threshold, canary.rollback.budget) and tenant opt-in control for Dedicated/Private installs.

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests for probe scheduler and budgeter logic.
- Integration tests simulate: (a) 30% sudden shift to long-sequence traffic (should attribute to WORKLOAD), (b) increased P95 under probes only (should attribute to MODEL), (c) transient GPU warmup pattern (should attribute to RUNTIME).
- Puppeted canary run in perf lab validated that automatic rollback is gated by attribution score and that budgeter prevents immediate subsequent rollbacks.
- CI: added synthetic scenarios to perf_canary_pipeline; full run passed on feature branch before merge.

Rollout plan:
- Start as a disabled feature flag in main.
- Enable probing in internal dogfood for 72h (staged by region).
- After validating attribution precision >=70% and rollback budget behavior stable, enable opt-in for customers on Dedicated as a beta.

Checklist:
- [x] Scheduler and attribution core implemented
- [x] Rollback budgeter integrated with rollout controller
- [x] Unit & integration tests added
- [x] Console UI panel to inspect traces
- [x] Feature flags and opt-in plumbing
- [x] CI pipeline additions

Related: ENG-1893 (reduce spurious automatic rollbacks), ENG-2010 (canary attribution roadmap), SUP-7721 (customer-reported oscillation incidents).
